Thus, this dialect can be considered a transitional dialect between Ukrainian and Russian.

Knowledge.Description: Knowledge of the use of the Hebrew Script
Knowledge.LongDescription: The Hebrew abjad writes Hebrew from right to left, with optional marks for vowels and cantillation.
Knowledge.Name: Hebrew Script

Knowledge.Description: Knowledge of the use of the Arabic Script
Knowledge.LongDescription: The Arabic script and its extended letters are used for Uyghur alongside other regional standards.
Knowledge.Name: Arabic Script

Knowledge.Description: Knowledge of the use of the Sanskrit Script
Knowledge.LongDescription: This legacy-named script record represents the Devanagari abugida used for Hindi and many Sanskrit texts.
Knowledge.Name: Sanskrit Script

Knowledge.Description: Knowledge of the use of the Tamil Script
Knowledge.LongDescription: The Tamil abugida is used to write Tamil in South India and Sri Lanka.
Knowledge.Name: Tamil Script

Knowledge.Description: Knowledge of the use of the Telugu Script
Knowledge.LongDescription: The Telugu abugida is used to write Telugu.
Knowledge.Name: Telugu Script

Knowledge.Description: Knowledge of the use of the Thai Script
Knowledge.LongDescription: The Thai abugida writes Thai with consonant letters, dependent vowels and tone marks.
Knowledge.Name: Thai Script

Knowledge.Description: Knowledge of the use of the Khmer Script
Knowledge.LongDescription: The Khmer abugida writes Khmer with consonant series and dependent vowels.
Knowledge.Name: Khmer Script

Knowledge.Description: Knowledge of the use of the Lao Script
Knowledge.LongDescription: The Lao abugida writes Lao with consonant letters, dependent vowels and tone marks.
Knowledge.Name: Lao Script

Knowledge.Description: Knowledge of the use of the Javanese Script
Knowledge.LongDescription: The traditional Javanese abugida, descended from Kawi, writes Javanese.
Knowledge.Name: Javanese Script

Knowledge.Description: Knowledge of the use of the Traditional Mongolian Script
Knowledge.LongDescription: Traditional Mongolian is written vertically in columns running from left to right.
Knowledge.Name: Traditional Mongolian Script

Knowledge.Description: Knowledge of the use of the Tibetan Script
Knowledge.LongDescription: The Tibetan abugida is shared across the major written Tibetic traditions.
Knowledge.Name: Tibetan Script

Knowledge.Description: Knowledge of the use of the Tifinagh Script
Knowledge.LongDescription: Tifinagh is the consonantal script family historically associated with Amazigh languages and revived in modern standards.
Knowledge.Name: Tifinagh Script

Knowledge.Description: Knowledge of the use of the Latin Script
Knowledge.LongDescription: The Latin alphabet is adapted to many modern languages through diacritics and additional letters.
Knowledge.Name: Latin Script

Knowledge.Description: Knowledge of the use of the Cryllic Script
Knowledge.LongDescription: The Cryllic script is based on the Old Church Slavonic script and used by a variety of Slavic and former Soviet languages. There are small variations between languages to show sounds unique to that language but it is generally very similar across languages.
Knowledge.Name: Cryllic Script

Knowledge.Description: Knowledge of the use of the Greek Script
Knowledge.LongDescription: The Greek script was once widely used across the world but is nowadays mostly limited to the use of the Greek language and as a source of symbols for Mathematics.
Knowledge.Name: Greek Script

Knowledge.Description: Knowledge of the use of the Japanese Script
Knowledge.LongDescription: Japanese writing combines kana syllabaries with kanji logographs; katakana is also used to write the modern Ainu languages.
Knowledge.Name: Japanese Script

Knowledge.Description: Knowledge of the use of the Korean Script
Knowledge.LongDescription: The Korean script, also known as Hangul, is a featural alphabet arranged into syllable blocks.
Knowledge.Name: Korean Script

Knowledge.Description: Knowledge of the use of the Chinese Script
Knowledge.LongDescription: Chinese writing uses logographs shared across the written standards represented by Mandarin and Yue.
Knowledge.Name: Chinese Script

A given name is purposefully given, usually by a child's parents at or near birth, in contrast to an inherited one such as a family name. A given name is sometimes legally changed through a name change. Given names are often used in a familiar and friendly manner in informal situations. The idiom "on a first-name basis" (or "on first-name terms") alludes to the familiarity of addressing another by a given name.]]></Element>    <Element Usage="3" MinimumCount="0" MaximumCount="3" Name="Middle Name"><![CDATA[Middle names are normally chosen by parents at the same time as the first name. Surnames are also sometimes used as middle names, usually to honor a relative. A child is sometimes given a middle name that is the first or middle name of one of his or her parents.
